info.name: CSC456 - School Management API
info.description:
All routes of the School Management API. Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner: ids created by earlier requests are saved into collection variables and reused by later ones.

MongoDB/Mongoose: Teachers, Courses, Students (Course -> Teacher many-to-one, Students <-> Courses many-to-many).
SQLite/Sequelize: AuditLogs.

item.name: 1. Teachers (MongoDB)
item.description: Teacher is the "one" side of the many-to-one relationship Course -> Teacher.

exec: pm.test("Has _id and name", () => { pm.expect(t).to.have.property("_id"); pm.expect(t.name).to.eql("John Smith"); });

request.description: Negative test: Mongoose schema validation rejects the document.

exec: pm.test("All match department", () => pm.response.json().forEach(t => pm.expect(t.department).to.eql("Computer Science")));

item.name: 2. Courses (MongoDB)
item.description: Many-to-one: every Course references exactly one Teacher.

item.name: Create course - teacher does not exist

request.description: Negative test: the referenced teacher must exist.

item.name: Create course - credits out of range

exec: pm.test("Teacher is populated object", () => { const c = pm.response.json()[0]; pm.expect(c.teacher).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(c.teacher).to.have.property("name"); });
pm.test("Has teacher and students", () => { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.teacher).to.have.property("name"); pm.expect(c.students).to.be.an("array"); });

item.name: 3. Students & Enrollments (MongoDB)
item.description: Many-to-many: Students <-> Courses. The `courses` array lives on Student.

4. Audit Logs (SQLite)
item.description: Standalone SQL entity stored in SQLite with Sequelize. Rows are also written automatically by every create/update/delete above.

exec: pm.test("Has total and data", () => { const r = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(r.total).to.be.a("number"); pm.expect(r.data).to.be.an("array"); });
pm.test("All are Student ENROLL", () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(l => { pm.expect(l.entity).to.eql("Student"); pm.expect(l.action).to.eql("ENROLL"); }));
